title: sse-streaming: fix chunking/framing for partial JSON & delimiter ordering
author: Alex Nguyen
description:
Motivation: streaming SSE responses used by our OpenAI-compat layer could emit chunks in ways that broke partial-JSON consumers and tool/function-calling clients. We saw two classes of bugs: (1) partial JSON objects split across chunk boundaries where the JSON delimiter/state was not preserved, leading to parser errors in strict stream consumers; (2) incorrect ordering of token/event framing in edge cases when the runtime emitted both data and event frames rapidly (e.g. immediate function-calling token followed by final event), which could result in out-of-order events at the client. This PR consolidates framing logic, adds deterministic delimiter insertion for partial JSON sequences, and ensures event ordering guarantees for combined token+event emissions.
What I changed: consolidated SSE chunking/framing into a single well-tested module and made the following behavioral fixes:
- Ensure that when we detect a streaming structured output (partial JSON/object tokens), we emit a stable JSON delimiter prefix for the first chunk and apply an explicit continuation marker for all subsequent chunks until the object is complete. This reduces ambiguity for streaming JSON parsers.
- Introduce a tiny state machine to serialize token frames vs event frames so that token data is always emitted before associated terminal events (e.g. done/error) in the same logical step.
- Fix race where streaming goroutines could reorder frames under high throughput by adding a bounded in-order output queue and backpressure path for sync points (cheap contention-free ring buffer on hot path).
- Update the OpenAI compatibility layer (sdk/python/openai_compat) to accept the new delimiter semantics and provide a compatibility shim when the client requests legacy framing.
- Add comprehensive unit and integration tests that simulate fragmented JSON token boundaries and high-concurrency emission patterns.
Checklist:
- [x] Add unit tests for sse framing state machine
- [x] Add integration test against openai_compat SSE consumer
- [x] Backward compatible: legacy clients can opt into previous framing via header "X-Redwood-SSE-Compat: legacy"
- [x] Add docs note in openai-compat.md and changelog
- [x] Run perf canary to measure latency/regressions
Testing and CI: initial run uncovered a flaky test in tests/integration/test_sse_streaming.py (timing-sensitive), fixed by converting to a deterministic wait on the framing completion hook instead of sleep. Full CI now passes. Manual canary on staging for a 24h window showed no regressions and slight reduction in parse errors for streaming consumers.
Backwards compatibility: default behavior is improved framing. To minimize customer impact, we added a header-based compatibility shim and a rollout flag that will be flipped in the config controller after a 1-week canary.
Notes for reviewers: the main behavioral logic lives in rust/crates/runtime/src/sse.rs; python shim is a thin translation layer. Pay attention to the in-order queue implementation and the tests in tests/unit/test_sse_state_machine.rs which document the expected frame sequences. The change is performance-sensitive; I profiled critical hot paths and ensured allocations are minimized. Related: ENG-4321 (streaming stability epic), ENG-4387 (openai-compat streaming fixes).
